sections.heading: What is the K-Way Merge Pattern?
sections.content: K-Way Merge combines K sorted lists, arrays or streams into one sorted result, or finds the Kth smallest element across them. Instead of merging two lists at a time or concatenating everything and sorting, you keep a min heap that holds the current front element of each list. Repeatedly remove the smallest from the heap and push the next element from the same list. With N total elements this takes O(N log K).

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: You are given K sorted arrays, lists or matrix rows
Merge K sorted linked lists into one
Find the Kth smallest element across sorted lists or a sorted matrix
Find the smallest range that covers elements from every list
Find pairs with the smallest sums from two sorted arrays
Merge sorted streams or files too large to fit in memory
Keywords: K sorted, merge, sorted matrix, smallest range, kth smallest across lists

sections.heading: The Core Idea
sections.content: Each sorted list already has its smallest value at the front. The overall smallest value must therefore be one of the K fronts. A min heap gives you the smallest front in O(log K). After you take it, the next candidate from that same list becomes a new front, so you push it in. Each of the N elements is pushed and popped once, so the total cost is O(N log K).

Merge Two Sorted Lists Is the Building Block
sections.content: Almost every K-way merge idea reduces to merging two sorted sequences with two pointers. The heap simply picks the next list to take from, and divide and conquer repeats the two-list merge in rounds. If you are comfortable with mergeTwo, you can solve most of the problems in this topic.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Pushing all N elements into the heap at the start, which gives O(N log N) space and time
Forgetting to push the next element from the same list after a pop
Not storing the list index and element index in the heap entry
Pushing null nodes into the heap (check node != null before adding)
Comparing nodes without a comparator, which throws ClassCastException
Skipping empty lists or arrays when building the initial heap
Not handling K = 0, an empty input array, or a list of only empty lists
Subtracting values in the comparator, which can overflow (use compareBy)

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: K-way merge uses a min heap holding one front element from each sorted list
Pop the smallest, then push the next element from the same list
Time is O(N log K) and the heap holds at most K items
Divide and conquer gives the same time without a heap
Many problems (sorted matrix, pair sums, smallest range) are a hidden K-way merge
Always store which list and which index each heap element came from
